required_tuples.rationale: The minified book library lists exactly its five fixture items and reports their total.
GET items answers the list envelope (echoed query, total, offset) with minified items whose fields match the fixture book, whatever the minified flag.
GET items without a token is 401, and an unknown library id is 404 for an unrestricted user.
A negative or fractional limit or page is rejected with 400 before any query runs.
A user limited to the podcast library gets 403 on the book library items, even for an unknown id, and 200 on its own library.
Every sort key of the client's book sort menu, ascending and descending, yields the exact fixture order, and sort/desc are echoed.
Sorting by finishedAt puts the only finished book first, random keeps all five items, and an unknown or podcast-only sort key still lists all five items.
With the server setting sortingIgnorePrefix on, title sort orders by the title without its leading article, and off again restores plain order.
limit and page slice the sorted list, total stays the full count, offset is page*limit, and a page past the end is empty.
limit=0 or no limit lists every item and a page without a limit has offset 0.

Every filter group the client sends (genres, tags, authors, series, narrators, publishers, publishedDecades, languages, progress, missing, tracks, ebooks, abridged, explicit, issues, feed-open, share-open) selects exactly the expected books, with total equal to the match count.
filter=recent lists the books created within the last 60 days.
Progress filters follow the requesting user: the finisher has only the first saga book finished, root has no progress at all.
An unknown filter group selects everything, a series filter naming an unknown series selects nothing, and series.no-series selects books without a series.
Filtering by a series orders by sequence (secondary default, or the sequence sort, ascending or descending) and each item carries its series sequence.
include=rssfeed,share adds rssFeed to items with an open feed for everyone and mediaItemShare to shared items for admins only; without include neither appears; include is echoed lower-cased.
collapseseries=1 shows only the first book of each series (by sequence) carrying collapsedSeries, sorts by series name, and counts the collapsed list.
Filtering by one series with collapseseries=1 lists that series' books by sequence, pages them with limit and page, and reports the full count as total.
The podcast library lists its podcast with author, genres, numEpisodes, rssFeed under include=rssfeed, and numEpisodesIncomplete counted per user.
With a second podcast, every podcast sort key of the client menu orders the two podcasts as expected.
The podcast filter groups genres, tags, languages, explicit, issues and feed-open select the expected podcasts, and book-only groups do not filter.
A user without explicit access never gets explicit books or podcasts in the lists, their totals or the explicit filter.
A user limited to the tag alpha sees only books tagged alpha, and a user with tag beta not accessible sees all books except those tagged beta.
Collapsing series respects the user's tag restriction: a series is represented by its first accessible book and counts of the collapsed list follow.
GET series answers the paged envelope with each series, its minified books ordered by numeric sequence, and totals.
Each series sort key of the client menu orders the three fixture series as expected, ascending and descending where the order has no ties.
With sortingIgnorePrefix on, name sort uses nameIgnorePrefix, so A Third Saga sorts after Solo Series.
limit and page slice the series list with the full total, and a page past the end is empty.

The series filter groups genres, tags, authors, narrators, publishers, languages and progress select the series with a matching book, per user for progress; the all filter and unknown filters select all.
The series list is 401 without a token, 404 for an unknown library, 403 outside the user's libraries and 400 for a negative limit.
Series lists show only series with a book the user may access and list only those books: explicit, tag-limited and tag-excluded users see different series and books.
GET library series/:id returns the series object without books, and include=progress adds the accessible book ids and the ones this user finished.
include=rssfeed adds rssFeed null for a series without feed and the minified feed once a feed is open for it.
Library series/:id is 401 without a token, 404 for an unknown series or one of another library, and 403 for a user without the library.
GET /api/series/:id returns the series object and include=progress lists the accessible book ids and the user's finished ones.
include=rssfeed on /api/series/:id gives rssFeed null without a feed and the open feed otherwise.
GET /api/series/:id is 401 without a token, 404 for an unknown id and 404 when the user may access none of the series' books.
For the listener the book library shows continue-listening, continue-reading, recently-added, recent-series, discover, listen-again and newest-authors with the expected entities, types and totals.
The finisher gets continue-series and listen-again from the finished first book and no explicit book, root without progress gets no continue or again shelves.
The podcast library shows continue-listening and listen-again episodes per user, newest-episodes and recently-added podcasts.
Personalized shelves are 401 without a token, 404 for an unknown library and 403 outside the user's libraries.
Shelves of a tag-limited user contain only accessible books, series and authors.
After the listener finishes the first saga book and starts the first book of the third saga, the continue, continue-series, discover and listen-again shelves follow.
Book search matches titles, subtitles and asin as books, and names as series, authors, narrators, tags and genres, case-insensitively and trimmed, with counts.
A query without matches returns every section empty, and limit caps each section's matches.
Search is 400 without q, with an empty q, with a repeated q or a negative limit, 401 without a token, 404 for an unknown library and 403 outside the user's libraries.
Podcast search matches podcast title and author as podcasts, episode titles as episodes carrying the recent episode, and tags and genres with counts.
Search hides items the user cannot access: explicit books and podcasts for a user without explicit access, books without the allowed tag, and series left with no accessible book.
PATCH /api/series/:id with name and description answers the updated series object and persists both on the series row.
Repeating the same PATCH answers 200 with the same object and leaves the row, including updatedAt, untouched.
After the rename the series list, both series routes, item lists and search show the new name.
PATCH /api/series/:id is 401 without a token, 404 for an unknown series or one with no accessible books, 403 without the update permission and 400 when no valid string field is sent.
A description-only PATCH, an empty description, a Unicode name and extra keys are accepted: only name and description change.
A rejected PATCH (no permission, invalid body, no accessible books) leaves the row unchanged, including updatedAt, and emits no series_updated event.
A PATCH that changes a series emits series_updated with the full series object to every authenticated socket (admin, user, library-restricted) and not to a connection that never authenticated.
Repeating a PATCH with unchanged values answers 200 but emits no series_updated.
A later change of only the description emits a new series_updated carrying the unchanged name and the new description.
A rejected PATCH (forbidden, invalid body, unknown series) emits no series_updated.
A quick match that creates a new series emits series_added with the new series object to every authenticated socket and not to an unauthenticated one.
Matching the same book again, also with overrideDetails, naming the existing series emits no series_added and creates no second row.
A second quick match naming another new series emits a second series_added for that series only.
Creating a series through the media update route creates the row but emits no series_added.
A quick match without provider results (warning), a forbidden match and a match of an unknown item emit no series_added.
Removing a series from its only book through the media update deletes the series and emits series_removed {id, libraryId} to every authenticated socket, not to an unauthenticated one.
Repeating the update that removes nothing emits no series_removed.
A series shared by two books survives the first removal without event and is removed, with the event, when the second book leaves it.
A quick match with overrideDetails that replaces a book's only series by an existing one removes the emptied series and emits series_removed, and no series_added.
A forbidden or unknown-item media update leaves the series in place and emits no series_removed.
Rescanning a book whose metadata file lists another series removes the emptied old series and emits series_removed (the new series gets no series_added).
Deleting the only book of a series removes the series and emits series_removed.
